The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind

The world is huge and the landscapes varied. Great for us explorer types. Each region had its own flavor, both in characters and architecture. No quest markers, or waypoints. You had to actually listen to the directions given. Reading the books in game would lead you to hidden treasure troves, assuming you realized it was a clue as it never shows up as a "quest" in your log book. You could create your own spells, which allowed varied combat and play styles. The game allowed you to "fail" by not having any un-killable NPCs. You could break quest lines, even destroy the gods themselves and the game just kept chugging along.

And this is all before you mod it up to look better (MGSO) or add more quests or continents to explore. Later games in the series may have some improvements to the combat system, but it was at the expense of everything else.

I think decentralization is a good idea. Let's assess the benefits we currently have from using an aggregating site like voat or reddit or pinterest.

  • niche and focused interest communities
  • straightforward and relatively easy-to-use standardized interface format
  • integrated private message function, consistent identity and contact method across the whole service
  • loads of new content (old content is not favored as much by current social media websites, which is a shame IMO)
  • Free, super easy to use - especially when combined with free image and video hosting services
  • pseudo-anonymous, pseudo-private - separate from our facebook accounts or real-life relationships and contacts, freedom to be honest, silly, dissenting, fake, a troll or jackass or retard
  • on reddit and voat, hierarchical discussion pages. on 4chan or 8chan, forums, slashdot, metafilter, etc. chronologically linear discussion threads
  • on reddit, voat, 8chan, the ability to create a space for posting/discussing whatever you could want, and the ability for others to easily interact in that space
  • leveraging the aggregating and sorting/evaluation power of a large community

I'm sure I'm overlooking some important things.

If we had some way to let users connect to each other in a decentralized network through an interface like this, I think it would be a good thing. It could be like bittorrent maybe with some kind of anonymizing pathing process to protect privacy. Maybe with a few hub servers that networks connect to? Maybe diaspora already works like this... i haven't tried it out. That's the other thing, diaspora is marketed kind of as a facebook alternative (when it is marketed at all), whereas voat and reddit and 8chan and pinterest are presented as services with communities or neat fresh interesting regular content.

I dunno. its super late here and I am probably rambling in a nonsensical way.
